messages:
maria: quick heads-up — spotted sustained saturation on primary model `redwood-8b` for several tier-2 tenants in us-east around 09:02. latency spikes + queue growth. thinking we should try a prefetch + soft-fallback flow rather than immediate hard swap. ideas?

sanjay: can you paste the metric slice? is this per-tenant burst or sustained?

maria: per-tenant but repeats across 4 tenants, ~3-6min bursts, avg queue length 90->260, p95 latency jumps to ~950ms. link: https://console.redwood/obs/query?id=abc123

olivia: sounds like capacity contention not misrouted traffic. prefetch sounds promising — what do you mean exactly by prefetch here?

maria: prefetch = when primary's input queue length > Q1 OR observed start-to-token-latency > L ms for X consecutive requests, we start routing a small % of new requests to `redwood-3b-quant` as a trial to warm KV caches and reduce tail. only ramp if trial success metrics (latency, error rate, "quality proxy") look OK.

kai: important: prefetch must not change billing semantics silently. product wants clear telemetry + cost attribution.

\maria: agreed. plan: tag fallback requests with header `X-RW-Fallback:soft-prefetch` so billing + telemetry can break down.

sanjay: how do we evaluate "quality proxy" cheaply? expensive evals aren't feasible on each request.
\olmarria: (typo) — olivia: maybe use a lightweight embedding similarity check on a sample of outputs? or compare token-level perplexity delta?
\kai: embedding similarity as a periodic probe sounds reasonable. also measure user-visible regression via our eval harness on canary traffic.

anna: console UX note: we should surface prefetch toggles per-tenant and show budget impact estimate (tokens and dollars) + rollback button. customers will freak if we silently switch models.

maria: agree. propose defaults: soft-prefetch off for tier-1, on for tier-2 with conservative thresholds, on by opt-in for self-serve. plus an account-level override: `force_primary_only`.

sanjay: API semantics question: do we expose fallback as a routing hint (user can opt-in) or keep it internal? if internal, product needs clear SLA docs.
\kai: internal-only is simpler to maintain (we control consistency). but product/ps want opt-in per-tenant. support both: internal policy engine + optional tenant opt-in header `X-RW-Allow-Fallback:true` that overrides policy.

olivia: implementation sketch (pseudo-config):
```json
{
  "fallback_policy": {
    "trigger": {"queue_len_gt": 100, "p95_ms_gt": 500, "consecutive":3},
    "strategy":"soft-prefetch",
    "initial_rate":0.03,
    "ramp_factor":2,
    "max_rate":0.25,
    "probe_checks":["latency","error_rate","embedding_similarity"]
  }
}
```

maria: perfect. two more enforcement questions: 1) tenant quotas — we must ensure prefetch doesn't blow reserved capacity for other tenants, 2) circuit-breaker — immediate revert if error_rate spikes > E%.

sanjay: quota enforcement: prefetch consumes a separate pool tag so accounting is explicit. if pool exhausted, backpressure to primary as before.
\kai: circuit-breaker: we can use rolling windows and abort on 5xx spike > 2% or embedding-similarity drop > 0.12. revert to primary-only and notify on-call.

olivia: telemetry — add these metrics: `fallback.trial_rate`, `fallback.success_rate`, `fallback.embedding_delta_p95`, `fallback.attributed_tokens` and expose per-tenant in console.

anna: also add a console banner when fallback kicks in: "Fallback active — some requests served by smaller model to meet latency SLOs. Click to see details and disable."

maria: rollout plan: feature-flagged in runtime, internal canary for infra team first (1% of traffic), then 5% of opt-in tiers, run for 48h, compare error/latency/cost impact, then wider.

kai: ops: add `deploy-bot` alerts for automatic revert. example message when circuit triggers:
`deploy-bot: [AUTO-REVERT] soft-prefetch reverted for tenancy acme-corp due to error_rate 3.2% (>2%).`

sanjay: one last concern — request affinity / sticky KV caches. if we route a request to fallback, might miss warmed KV state and actually be slower. prefetch should target new independent requests or use sticky routing for sessions.

maria: good call. we'll exclude requests with `session_id` header from prefetch ramp and prefer sticky routing there.

olivia: ok i'm happy with this direction. I'll mock the dashboard panels and probes for embedding similarity.

anna: I'll add UX mocks and copy for the banner + per-tenant toggle.

maria: thanks all — i'll draft a short design doc and a small prototype change for the runtime flag. tagging @kai for alert wiring.

kai: got it, I'll wire the alert and add runbook steps.
\ndeploy-bot: [INFO] canary rollout scheduled: `soft-prefetch` feature-flag enabled for infra-team at 1709015600.
